changeability.rationale: Data-level fixes (sprites, card mapping, table columns) land in one obvious, well-named place; the duplicated card-grid markup and the double-encoded team query are the main places where a fix must be applied twice.

evidence: app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:46-56 — PageData.load handles the real variation (TransferState hydration on first load, loader fetch afterwards) in one reusable service

app/src/app/pages/team/team-page.ts:73-99 — hand-rolled async reload with effect + loadId race guard re-implements what resource/httpResource would give for free; this is the hardest component to modify safely

app/src/app/shared/card-list.ts:11 vs app/src/app/pages/home/home.html:36 vs app/src/app/pages/team/team-page.ts:25 — three copies of the card grid (pagination and remove-buttons justify two, but home and CardList overlap)
abstraction_design.rationale: The VM + loader + shared-component pattern is designed around the app's real variation and stretches cleanly to a new Items section; deductions are for the three inlined card grids and the team page's hand-rolled reactive loading.

findings.issue: Card grid markup is duplicated across home.html, shared/card-list.ts and team-page.ts, so any card-level behavior change (sorting, new badge) must be implemented twice or thrice.
findings.suggestion: Extend CardList with optional inputs (e.g. priority offset, extra per-item content via ng-content or a template) and have Home use it for the paged slice.

findings.issue: Caching rules are split across two independent caches with separate TTLs (client cache here, server cache in server/api-client.ts) plus a Cache-Control header in src/server.ts:25, so a policy change touches three files.
findings.suggestion: Name both TTLs from a single shared constant/module (or fold client caching into PageData configuration) so the policy is stated in one place.

findings.issue: The API base URL default 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated as a literal here and in server/api-client.ts:13; changing the default (or the env var name) requires two edits.
findings.suggestion: Export a single DEFAULT_API_BASE from server/api-client (or a tiny shared config module) and reference it from both.

findings.issue: Team reload is hand-rolled with effect + loadId race guard + linkedSignal instead of resource/httpResource, which is subtle and easy to break when extending (e.g. adding team editing).
findings.suggestion: Re-express the client-side team VM as a resource() keyed on team.names(), deleting the manual race-guard logic.

findings.issue: The /team data-path query encoding is written in both the route resolver and team-page.ts:97, an implicit contract duplicated across files.
findings.suggestion: Extract a buildTeamPath(names) helper into data/page-data.ts (or a team-data module) used by both call sites.

findings.issue: The Abilities section lives inside another page's template, so removing the abilities feature edits an unrelated page.
findings.suggestion: Extract page sections into small components in the pokemon feature folder so removal is per-section deletion.

findings.issue: Title strategy duck-types route.data['vm'] and a 'notFound' flag, coupling it to every resolver's key-naming convention.
findings.suggestion: Standardize on a typed route-data interface (e.g. a PageData interface with title?: string) documented next to the pageData() resolver factory.

findings.issue: The search box's URL-following logic depends on a mutable pushedQ side-channel inside a linkedSignal computation, which is correct but hard to reason about for future editors.
findings.suggestion: Add a reference to the linkedSignal 'previous state' doc pattern in a comment, or model in-flight search as its own signal merged in the computation.

summary: This is a well-factored codebase: pages consume typed view models through one uniform route/resolver/loader pattern, server and client code are separated by a genuine injection seam, and shared components carry the real reuse. Data-level bug fixes (sprites, card mapping, move-table columns) land in single obvious places. The main editability costs are three inlined copies of the card grid, caching and base-URL knowledge spread across a few files, and the team page's hand-rolled reactive loading — all fixable without redesign.
